questionsApplications.label: How can prevention improve population health fairly?
How do behaviour, institutions and environment affect health?

alternatives.concept: A programme connecting epidemiology and prevention with health psychology, lifespan development, biological disease mechanisms, social inequalities and environmental justice. Quantitative, qualitative and evidence-synthesis methods support inquiry, while public economics, organisational psychology and policy analysis examine collective responses. It does not reproduce the Dutch healthcare curriculum or the final supervised placement and thesis.

alternativeSelection.assessment: One substantive population-health/behaviour/policy programme passes for the confirmed core. Hospital organisation is addressed through specific policy, economics and organisational contributions, with Dutch care-system gaps explicit; those actual contributions do not supply additional specialist healthcare-management progression for a distinct full alternative. Health-app privacy is separately tested and lacks sustained specialist content. Career/illustrative rows do not generate programmes.

notes.text: UCR offers broader population-health, behavioural and policy inquiry. It provides less dedicated Dutch/international healthcare organisation and implementation research, and does not reproduce the VU supervised placement, professional-development sequence or required health-science thesis.

audience.programmeDescription: Health Sciences examines population health and wellbeing through biological, behavioural, social and policy perspectives. The confirmed early curriculum studies health inequalities, lifestyle and environment, health systems, prevention and health across the lifespan.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The confirmed population-health, behavioural, lifespan and research-methods core supports a meaningful broader UCR programme in population health, behaviour and social policy; the unverified final-year research/professional culmination is outside this comparison. UCR supplies actual epidemiological, health-psychological and empirical inquiry with biological and policy complements. Dedicated care-system and implementation depth differs; the final VU research placement and required endwork are not reproduced.

curriculum.limitation: The nominal VU degree is 180 EC. The displayed 150 EC comprise the confirmed first two years and at least 30 EC of minor/elective study. The revised-cohort allocation of the final 30 EC, including later methods, professional development, research placement and thesis, is not verified.
